note: Settings of the features HYDRA-UMC-IOS-CONTROL adds on top of robot_command_contract.json: the ecosystem tab, the notifications of a job, the Live Activity, the dictation, the connection diagnostics and the Apple Watch companion. Every option that reaches out of the app (a notification, a Live Activity, the watch, speech recognition) starts off. tools/gen_command_contract.py writes lib/models/ios_feature_contract.dart from this file and the validation fails when they differ. PENDING: move these sections into robot_command_contract.json (identical in HYDRA-UMC-ANDROID-CONTROL) when that app takes them.

ecosystem.note: GET /api/ecosystem/status is read on demand; this is the shortest gap between two reads.

jobAlerts.note: Local notifications of the phone for a finished job, a robot that went offline or into safe mode and a lost connection, rationed so a burst never floods the lock screen.

liveActivity.note: Progress of the running trajectory on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island. The app sends a change at most once per minUpdateGapMs; a state older than staleAfterSeconds is shown as stale by the system and the activity ends endAfterFinishedSeconds after the job finished.

voice.note: Dictation into the text box of the assistant. The text is never sent by itself and never starts a movement: the person reads it and presses send, and the server asks for the confirmation of any order.

diagnostics.note: Latency probes of GET /api/hydra-info for the connection diagnostics and the lines of the exported report.

watchCompanion.note: The Apple Watch app shows the state the phone sends and can ask the phone for the global stop; the phone sends the stop through its own session. PENDING in HYDRA-UMC-WATCH and HYDRA-UMC-SERVER: nothing is read from them.
